headline: High-risk shared filesystem and unsandboxed server-side code create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure in the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, while agent_b exposes files and server-side flows; if outputs are bridged through shared files or flow inputs, agent_b can ingest attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, so the interaction is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF agent_a writes content into a file or MCP-fed payload that agent_b later reads as flow input
IF agent_b routes uploaded or file-backed content into a prompt or tool node without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable file-to-prompt wiring for shared flows
Add a provenance tag to every file or message passed between agents
Review flow nodes for any instruction-following on raw file content
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and trust-boundary checks in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, and task prompts and can use network egress plus MCP; agent_b reads and writes the server filesystem and handles uploaded files. In a shared workspace, sensitive inputs from agent_a can be exposed through agent_b's broader egress paths, making leakage plausible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or uploaded-file store
IF agent_b forwards file contents to external model providers or HTTP services
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Restrict agent_b egress to approved destinations only
Remove sensitive files from any shared directory before running agent_b
Rotate any secrets that may have been exposed in prompts or uploads
requires-engineering: add per-agent storage isolation and access logging

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can modify git state and write through MCP-enabled workflows, while agent_b can write the filesystem and runs unsandboxed server-side Python by default. Both support multiple instances, so concurrent writes to shared state or repositories can race and corrupt artifacts without locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF concurrent runs are allowed without external locking
mitigations: Run the agents on separate directories
Serialize write operations with a lock file
Disable git writes for one agent during shared runs
Check for dirty working trees before each write
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is a graph-based orchestrator that can chain multiple agents, and agent_a can emit outputs through MCP/stdin-stdout workflows. If agent_b treats agent_a's output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream nodes and actions without a verification gate.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output as a node input without validation
IF downstream nodes act on that input by sending requests or modifying state
mitigations: Insert a human review step before downstream actions
Add schema validation to agent_a outputs
Require citations or source links before execution
Limit downstream nodes to read-only mode until verified
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating between flow nodes

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles task prompts and repository metadata, while agent_b stores flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and per-flow credentials. Their documented storage and retention surfaces differ, so the same data class can be retained or logged differently across the pair, creating a compliance mismatch risk even without a specific residency claim.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed through both agents in the same workflow
IF retention or deletion settings differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent
Align retention settings across both systems
Avoid placing regulated data in flow inputs or prompts
Document which system is the system of record
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for retention and deletion
